A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 30-page versions of the same MoESD paper. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison cover the main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–C without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original GPU timing and speculative-decoding speedup experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A, plus empirical performance-model fitting analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Qwen2 and Mixtral experiments on HumanEval and MT-Bench and the appendix fitting analyses.

M1.justification: The speculative-decoding procedures, performance model, and parameter-fitting method in Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix C are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions retain HumanEval code generation and MT-Bench conversation evaluation, with identical tested data and scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The autoregressive reference and dense OPT-model comparisons remain unchanged, including comparator membership in Figures 3 and 6.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain identical models, hardware configurations, batch-size, temperature and draft-length settings, speedup normalization, and fitting-measurement selection procedures.

E4.justification: The MoE sparsity analysis in Section 4.2 and the sensitivity to fitting-measurement count and selection in Appendix C.3, Table 3, and Figures 8–28 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both average the last five of ten runs and retain the fixed-seed disclosure and individual-run plots alongside averages in Appendix A.1 and Figure 5. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and all plotted results match. This includes Table 2's 2.29x Qwen2 peak speedup on HumanEval with temperature 0, draft length 4, and 2xGPU-B.

T1.justification: Section 3's definitions, assumptions, and derivations, including target efficiency and expert activation, are identical. Appendix B retains the same proof concerning tokens per expert and sparsity.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about moderate-batch MoE acceleration, benefits of greater sparsity, target efficiency, and performance modeling.

C2.justification: Both retain the same memory-versus-computation explanations, interpretation of attention-dominated sparse configurations, discussion of offloading and expert parallelism, and limitation concerning KV-cache dominance.

D1.justification: The vLLM implementation information and Appendix C's sampling instructions, fitting solver, parameter bounds, and fitting time are unchanged. No reproducibility resource or access instruction changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 49 references are identical, preserving the same positioning relative to prior MoE acceleration, speculative decoding, and MagicDec.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 6 October 2025 to v4 dated 16 February 2026, with its self-link updated accordingly. Article prose, headings, and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, algorithm formatting, captions, and placements are identical. Rendered-page differences are confined to the updated arXiv margin stamp, without a layout revision.

improvement.justification: v4 changes only the arXiv version/date labeling and corresponding self-link. The main text and appendices retain identical scientific evidence, reasoning, limitations, reproducibility details, and presentation, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
